data.description:
On Tuesday, the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) closed with a 0.46% loss, while the Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ) fell 0.65%. U.S. stocks faced pressure after the 10-year Treasury yield rose 4.5 basis points to 5%, marking its highest level since 2007.

News That Moved the Stock Market Today

  • With higher yields, the opportunity cost of owning equities rises. Elevated yields also raise borrowing costs and reduce the present value of future cash flows.
  • The Fed is set to announce its interest rate decision tomorrow at 2 p.m. Eastern Time. Traders assign a 94.5% probability that the central bank will raise rates by 25 bps, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The last time the Fed raised rates was July 2023.
  • Since 2008, the Fed has always hiked rates when the implied probability of a hike exceeds 90% one day before a decision, according to Bloomberg.
  • White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett noted that the Fed shouldn't raise rates because inflation is easing. He added President Trump would "100% support" the central bank's decision.
  • Wells Fargo (WFC) lowered its year-end S&P 500 (SPX) price target to 7,700 from 7,950. The firm believes that the midterms present a risk to equities, "especially as political pushback against data centers continues to gain ​momentum."
  • Robinhood (HOOD) closed in the red after two of its employees were charged with fraud. The employees allegedly used stolen information to trade perpetual futures.
  • Meta Platforms (META) is preparing to use proprietary AI chips in its data centers starting in early 2027.
  • Oil stocks rose alongside rising Brent crude oil (BZ) prices, with Chevron (CVX), Exxon Mobil (XOM), and Marathon Petroleum (MPC) closing in the green.

data.title: S&P 500 Top Stock Gainers Today, 9/15/26
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) closed with a 0.45% loss on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields continued to pressure equities. The 10-year yield rose 4.5 basis points to 5%, its highest level since 2007. In addition, the Fed is set to announce its interest rate decision tomorrow at 2 p.m. Eastern Time. Energy led all sectors with a 2.26% gain, while consumer discretionary stocks lagged with a 1.76% loss.

Let's break down the sectors behind the performance.

Today's Top-Performing Sector 

Energy was the top-performing sector as Brent crude oil (BZ) rose 2.5% to $108 per barrel. Earlier this week, Saudi Arabia said it had closed its East-West oil pipeline due to damages caused by drone strikes. Oil supply could fall by 120 million barrels if the pipeline remains closed for a month, according to Kpler. However, that would benefit oil companies, as lower supply tends to push prices higher.

data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Ticks Up With New British Ad Deal
data.description:
Entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY) is actually a bigger part of British television than you might think. It owns Paramount UK network 5, previously known as Channel 5. That network recently struck up a deal with Channel 4 over advertising that is being hailed by Deadline as "historic." Investors were happy enough about the arrangement, and sent Paramount shares up modestly in the closing minutes of Tuesday's trading. Paramount has seen a 38.28% loss in its share price over the past year.

A Fairly Big Deal

The deal calls for Channel 4 and the former Channel 5 to get together on advertising. Channel 4 Sales will become the leading partner for a wide range of Paramount brands in the United Kingdom under the terms of the deal. Channel 4 will handle ad sales for MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon, the kids' block Milkshake!, and several Channel 5 sub-brands like 5USA, 5Star, and 5Action. This is actually the first time in British television history that two public service broadcasters are joining together in such fashion.

Paramount and Comcast's (CMCSA) Sky had an advertising deal together previously, but that deal runs out at the end of this year. Reemah Sakaan, head of 5, noted, "5 is on an incredible run, delivering must-watch hits that draw large, loyal audiences across every platform. Combine that momentum with Channel 4's commercial strength, and advertisers get a scale and targeting proposition they won't find anywhere else."

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Slides as 2027's F-150 Emerges
data.description:
So we know that legacy automaker Ford (F) is heavily dependent on the F-150 for its overall sales. So when talk of the next model year's version emerges, it is worth paying attention to. However, new reports from Car and Driver detailing the 2027 F-150 have not been met with the kind of response you might expect. Investors sent Ford shares down over 2% in Tuesday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 19.38% rally in its share price over the past year.

Big New Pickup

The 2027 F-150 has had its official reveal, and there is quite a bit of change afoot. Earlier reports that suggested the change was coming were proven correct, as the 2027 F-150 will get a new grille, new wheel designs, a new base engine, and an upgraded version of BlueCruise, Ford's hands-free driving assistance tool.

However, Ford also released pricing on these new models. The 2027 F-150 Raptor will be priced a bit lower than the 2026, $4,010 less in fact. But that still starts it at $77,790. The 2027 F-150 Tremor, meanwhile, will come in at $62,440, which is a $5,270 markdown from the 2026 equivalent. For those willing to go down to the base F-150, it starts at $42,630.

data.title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Is Falling on Tuesday – Here's Why
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) said Tuesday that it cannot restore access to certain customer data stored in parts of the Persian Gulf after several of its cloud facilities were damaged during the U.S.-Iran war. The company shared the update on its Amazon Web Services (AWS) health page, noting that the affected information was hosted only in data centers in Bahrain and in parts of its network in the United Arab Emirates. Following the news, AMZN stock was down about 2% on Tuesday.

AWS said the Bahrain sites were hit early in the conflict, with damage beyond what the company's systems were built to handle. Satellite images later showed strikes on two facilities there.

Most customers in Bahrain shifted their workloads to other countries after the first strikes in March, and further damage in April wiped out the remaining data center network in the country. In the UAE, Amazon said many customers were able to restore operations by using backups or copying data that stayed reachable. However, the company still cannot access data stored in one UAE availability zone, and engineers are working to recover resources in two others.

Other Factors Pressuring the Stock

On the logistics side, Amazon filed an 8‑K with the SEC saying it has paused work with air carrier 21 Air. The move follows a deadly crash of an Amazon‑branded cargo plane in Miami. The pause only affects a small slice of Amazon's Prime Air network, but active federal safety probes add short‑term shipping and reputational pressure that is weighing on the stock.

Further, the wider tech sector is under pressure after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that frontier AI work is slowing. That comment hit harder for Amazon, which recently raised its full‑year 2026 capex guide to $220 billion, most of it aimed at AI data centers and custom chips.

With spending now running far above earlier plans, investors are concerned that such huge cash outlays may take longer to produce real returns.

data.title: Why Is DataMeds AI Stock (MEDS) Up Nearly 200% Today?
data.description:
DataMeds AI (MEDS) stock rocketed higher on Tuesday after the health IT company announced its acquisition of a business from Axe Compute (AGPU). Axe Compute sold its legacy cancer diagnostics business, Helomics Corporation, to DataMeds AI. The deal moves Helomics out of Axe Compute as the company completes its shift to a pure-play neocloud GPU-as-a-Service business.

Under the terms of the deal, Axe Compute sold its wholly owned Helomics unit in return for DataMeds AI common shares and common share equivalents. Helomics is a Pittsburgh-based precision medicine platform focused on cancer care. The company uses AI and real-world tumor data to aid drug discovery and cancer treatment choices. Helomics was the last operating business left from Axe Compute's prior identity as Predictive Oncology Inc. Axe Compute changed its name in December 2025 as part of its move toward AI compute services.

The sale also gives DataMeds AI a new role in oncology. The company claimed that the deal adds Helomics' cancer data and AI tools to its platform. DataMeds AI said it plans to use its data-driven approach to help improve patient outcomes in an area with a high need for better care.

data.title: Target (TGT) to Challenge on Amazon's Fall Sales Event
data.description:
Discount retailer Target (TGT) is looking to challenge Amazon's (AMZN) autumn Prime Days sales event. Minneapolis-based Target has announced that its fall "Circle Deal Days" event will run Oct. 6–7 in a direct challenge to Amazon's "Prime Big Deal Days" shopping extravaganza. Target said in a statement that it will offer discounts of up to 40% on thousands of products during he October event.

Target's promotions will cover fall apparel, home décor, kitchen tools, beauty products, toys, technology, and holiday merchandise. The biggest discounts will be offered to Target Circle 360 members, who can begin shopping select offers on Oct. 5. Target added that its strategy with the fall sales event is to attract budget-conscious seasonal shoppers.

Taking on Amazon

Target (TGT) is also using the upcoming event to drive subscriptions to its Target Circle 360 loyalty rewards program. The autumn sales event has evolved from Target Circle Week, a longer loyalty-sale format. In October 2025, Target held a seven-day Circle Week sales promotion that featured discounts of up to 50% and daily deals. That event proved popular with consumers.
